meta.title: IWE Code — Edit, compare, deploy
meta.description: A native workspace for editing local and server files, comparing changes, and deploying over SFTP, FTP or FTPS. With Git, pipelines and a terminal.

features.title:

items.title: Edit local and server files
items.description: Write with syntax highlighting, undo changes, and save when ready. Unsaved changes stay visible in your tabs.

items.title: Deploy with a clear destination
items.description: Connect through SFTP, FTP, or FTPS. Map folders, exclude paths, and choose a deployment profile for each project.

items.title: Follow changes in Git
items.description: Browse branches and commits. Compare file versions side by side and manage changes across your project repositories.

items.title: Keep track of pipelines
items.description: Connect GitHub Actions or GitLab. Inspect runs, stages, and jobs alongside the project they belong to.

items.title: Use a terminal in context
items.description: Open a terminal in your project. Run commands without leaving the workspace, then collapse the panel when finished.

items.title: Organize work into spaces
items.description: Group projects by team or task. Keep deployment profiles within each space and reuse connections across the editor.

workflow.title:
See the change.

items.title: Compare both versions

items.title: Keep working during transfers
items.description: Uploads and downloads run in the background. Check their progress without reopening the deployment panel.

items.question: Is IWE Code a code editor?
items.answer: Yes. IWE Code supports editing and saving local and server text files. Git revisions and comparison views remain read-only.

items.question: Do I need to move my projects?
items.answer: No. Add existing local folders to your workspace. IWE Code keeps their folder structure.

items.question: Can I use it without a GitHub account?
items.answer: Yes. Browse local projects and Git history without signing in. Private pipelines and job actions require a connected provider account.

items.question: Which languages can I use?
items.answer: The application and this website support English, Russian, and Spanish.

items.question: Does deployment upload files automatically?
items.answer: No. You choose when to upload, download, or save a server file. Downloading over existing local files requires confirmation.

items.question: Can I turn off modules?
items.answer: Yes. Git, pipelines, deployment, and terminal modules start enabled. You can disable each module in settings.
